t: GOKU CHARGES: TAP TO DODGE, OR YUJI'S HEAD BURSTS - OR THE WALL BEHIND HIM BREAKS
n: The Goku scene now goes on after Yuji's useless punch. Goku jumps back, lands, and charges at Yuji's head. Time slows down and the same ring as in chapter 5 closes on Yuji's head: tap the screen or press any key just when it closes to DODGE. You can be a little early or a little late (a tap right on time says PERFECT; too early says TOO EARLY).

If you do not dodge, Goku's fist hits Yuji's head and it bursts: with GRAPHIC DAMAGE on FULL you see blood, bits of hair and bone and the neck spurting while the body falls; on CLEAN the blow is the same but there is no blood; on OFF the picture just goes black. Then the words YUJI DIED come up and the scene starts again from just before Goku charges, so you can try again as often as you like.

If you dodge, Yuji ducks his head under the fist and the punch goes on into the wall behind him: a flash, the wall breaks open with stones, glass and dust, and a big hole stays in it. Goku stands in the dust looking at Yuji, then comes TO BE CONTINUED and you are back in the chapter list. A building now stands behind Yuji from the moment Goku arrives. With SETTINGS > no flashes the flashes go through black instead of white.

t: GOKU: INSTANT TRANSMISSION, "WHO ARE YOU?" AND A PUNCH INTO A BUILDING
n: You asked for Goku, with your picture of him. Now, after Yuji arrives in West City, the screen goes dark and you see Goku standing on a grassy hill, with the city far away behind him. He feels a strange power, puts two fingers on his forehead and uses instant transmission: a flash of light, a pillar of light where he stood, and the hill is empty.

Back in West City he is suddenly next to Yuji with his open hand held out, and he asks WHO ARE YOU? Yuji punches him with a normal punch and it does absolutely nothing: a dull thud, no spark, Yuji's arm shakes against him. Then Goku draws his fist back and punches Yuji: the screen flashes and shakes, Yuji is thrown across the street and slams into a building, which cracks, loses its windows and fills the air with dust and stones. The scene ends on TO BE CONTINUED and you are back in the chapter list.

Goku is drawn in pixel art like your picture: the spiky black hair, the orange gi with the blue undershirt, sash and wristbands, the blue boots. The only words are his line in the dialogue box and the TO BE CONTINUED card. With SETTINGS > no flashes the flashes go through black instead of white.

t: THE END OF THE CHAPTER 5 FIGHT: YUJI IS SENT TO WEST CITY
n: You asked for the story to go on after Yuji beats Iron Man. Now, when Iron Man's health runs out in the chapter 5 fight, the fight is over: your controls and the bars go away, the building starts to shake, dust falls and the lights flicker. Iron Man looks at Yuji, backs off a little and raises his palm: the charge in it grows and grows, but he never gets to fire.

Then a violet circle opens under Yuji, the same way he was sent to the MCU, and a column of violet light closes round him. The screen goes white and Yuji arrives in another universe, where the city is WEST CITY. It is drawn in pixel art from your pictures: silver domes, white towers with coloured tops, balls on stilts, a red monorail with a train on it, a blimp, palm trees, a crossing and a green road sign with the name of the city. After a few seconds the screen goes black and you are back in the chapter list. There are no words in the scene except the name on the sign. With SETTINGS > no flashes the change goes through black instead of white and the lights do not flicker.

t: FREDDY, RYU AND IRON MAN ARE BOUGHT IN THE SHOP, WITH THEIR MOVES
n: You asked for every character that was not in the shop to be buyable with his moves. Freddy, Ryu and Iron Man were free for everybody; now they are in SKILLS > CHARACTERS: FREDDY KRUEGER $2500, RYU $2800 and IRON MAN $3500. Every save starts with them locked: on the fighter screen of the BATTLE their faces say LOCKED (as your fighter and as the enemy) until you buy them. TRAINING stays free for all three, with every move, like it is for Yuji, Verity and the Cat.

Each of them has a page of his own in the shop now, with a tab of his own (FREDDY, RYU, IRON MAN), like Sukuna's: walking, jumping and the blows of the ATTACK chain stay free, and every other move is a node that you buy with money after the character. FREDDY (9 nodes): CROUCH, DASH, BLOCK, FAR PUNCHES, BOILING WATER, PIERCE, GROUND SLAM, NIGHTMARE, FATALITY. RYU (17): CROUCH, LEG KICK, DASH, BLOCK, DOWNSLAM, HARD PUNCH, FRONT KICK, POWER PUNCH, DIVE PUNCH, 5-HIT COMBO, DASH KICK, GRANITE MODE, GRANITE BLAST, DOUBLE BLAST, TRIPLE BLAST, JUST THIS ONCE, FATALITY. IRON MAN (16): CROUCH, LOW JABS, DASH, CHARGE PUNCH, BACKFLIP, BLOCK, ROCKET UPPERCUT, DOWNSLAM, BEAR HUG, GROUND PUNCH, REPULSOR MODE, BLAST, LASER, SPIN BLAST, UNIBEAM, FATALITY.

A move you have not bought is simply not there: its button is dimmed and pressing it says LOCKED: BUY IT IN SKILLS. The enemy Freddy, Ryu and Iron Man always have every move. The shop's top bar now holds nine tabs and goes onto a second line on a small screen.

t: YUJI'S ONE FATALITY FOR EVERYONE, THE ENEMY SUKUNA'S HEAD-CUT ON YOU, AND VERITY AND FREDDY ON SUKUNA, RYU AND IRON MAN
n: You asked for the missing fatalities and here they are. YUJI: all his separate versions for each enemy are gone, and he now has ONE fatality, the same on every enemy (the 30-second scene of eight BLACK FLASHES, the last one huge), like everybody else. And now the ENEMY YUJI does it to YOU too, from SEMI-GRADE 1 up, the moment you are at 20% or less and he is close: the whole picture is turned round and you are the one who takes the eight Black Flashes. In the training ADMIN box the enemy Yuji has a FINISHER button now.

SUKUNA: the enemy Sukuna now does his head-cut finisher to YOU, the same one you do to the enemy. You are held and kneel, he puts a hand in your hair and says "You hold your head quite high", a huge slash passes over your head, you stare up at him and charge, he touches your face and is gone, behind you, your head falls apart in three slices, a slow-motion replay shows that he touched you first, and then you fall. It works against every fighter, and it follows GRAPHIC DAMAGE: FULL shows the slices and the blood, CLEAN the slices without blood, OFF nothing is cut. Two taps skip it. He has a FINISHER button in the ADMIN box too.
VERITY AND FREDDY: their fatalities work on the enemy SUKUNA, RYU and IRON MAN now, and the enemy Verity and the enemy Freddy do theirs to you when you play Sukuna, Ryu or Iron Man: all four ways.
IRON MAN'S CARD on the fighter screen lists his FATALITY now, and it still fits inside the card.

t: IRON MAN'S FATALITY (FOR YOU AND FOR THE ENEMY IRON MAN) AND IRON MAN IN BATTLE
n: You asked for a FATALITY for Iron Man, beat by beat, and it is in the game now. When you play Iron Man the FATAL button is back: it lights up when the enemy is at 20% health or less and close, and it costs half of your cursed energy, like everybody's. The ENEMY IRON MAN does it to you as well, from SEMI-GRADE 1 up, the moment you are at 20% or less and he is close. It works against every fighter, on every map. There are no words in it, only the sounds and the word FATALITY at the end.

WHAT YOU WILL SEE (about 13 seconds): in a night street Iron Man crouches with his boots lit, then charges and carries the enemy through FOUR buildings with his fist in his stomach: every wall bursts with bricks, glass and dust, a tunnel is torn through each building, and the far wall bursts out the other side. He brakes and throws the enemy up. The camera follows him up: the street drops away, the stars and the MOON come in, and everything goes into SLOW MOTION with the enemy turning slowly in front of the moon.

THEN Iron Man comes up under him and BLASTS HIM IN THE BACK with the repulsor: the enemy arches, SCREAMS and spins. The blade comes out of Iron Man's forearm and he draws it back. Then THE DASH, as you said: 100 pixels in 0.01 seconds. It is faster than one picture of the screen, so he is on the screen for exactly ONE frame (a smear of him and a white line along the blade, whether your screen draws 60 or 120 pictures a second), and the very next frame the blade is already through the enemy. He pulls it out and throws the enemy off it, and the enemy falls.

THE KILL: the arc reactor in Iron Man's chest charges and he fires the UNIBEAM at the falling body: a white-out, then ONE frame of the enemy's SKELETON (an X-ray: the beam as a pale band, every bone white), and then he is ASH: every pixel of him lets go in turn, white-hot for a breath, then grey, then dark, and the beam blows them away. FATALITY, and the round is Iron Man's.

ONE THING I DECIDED, tell me if you want it the other way: the street, the buildings and the moon are drawn in the game for this scene, so it looks the same on every map (street or skyscraper). SETTINGS > GAME > GRAPHIC DAMAGE: FULL has the blood at the stab; CLEAN has no red; OFF turns the screen black from the dash until the ash is gone and only the sounds play. FLASHES (with REDUCED the skeleton is shown softly over the scene instead of as a black frame) and SHAKE in the settings are followed. In the training the ADMIN box has a FINISHER button for the enemy Iron Man.
ALSO: Iron Man is in the normal BATTLE now, as your fighter as well as the enemy: his face on the fighter screen no longer says TRAIN ONLY.

t: RYU'S FATALITY (FOR YOU AND FOR THE ENEMY RYU)
n: You asked for a FATALITY for Ryu, beat by beat, and it is in the game now. When you play Ryu the FATAL button is back: it lights up when the enemy is at 20% health or less and close, and it costs half of your cursed energy, like everybody's. The ENEMY RYU does it to you as well, from SEMI-GRADE 1 up, the moment you are at 20% or less and he is close. It works against every fighter, in the street and in the skyscraper.

WHAT YOU WILL SEE (about 19 seconds): Ryu charges, the enemy hops out of the way and Ryu's fist finds nothing, so it goes down into the ground. The ground cracks, the cracks run away along the road and a gap opens wide under both of them. They fall: the street slides away above them and a rock wall rushes past. Ryu catches the enemy by the ankles and says SWEET. CUT to a pixel picture of a tea table full of cakes: it starts on the pink berry cake in the middle and zooms out until the whole table is there, and then comes the crack of the knee and a crack runs through the picture. Back in the pit his back is folded and white cracks run out from his waist. They land, the enemy is thrown down, gets up on his knees and swings at Ryu, and Ryu does not even move.

THEN THE BARRAGE: blast after blast out of Ryu's hair into his face, with flashes and shaking, and the enemy burns to a black crust a little at a time. His right arm is blown into pixels that fly away and fall as ash, and a big hole is blown through his side. He falls over and says I THOUGHT YOU HAD ABANDONED THAT PRIDE. Then he starts YOU DISGUSTING ASS N- and it is cut off right after the N and the dash, exactly as you said, and he dies. FATALITY, and the round is Ryu's.

TWO THINGS I DECIDED, tell me if you want them the other way: (1) 'right' is the side you can see, so it is his near arm and the near side of his body that go. (2) The tea table is my pixel version of your picture, drawn in the game: a pink gingham cloth, the cake in the middle, a three-tier stand, a tart, a teapot, cups and a plate of little cakes. If you want it closer to your picture, tell me what to change.

SETTINGS > GAME > GRAPHIC DAMAGE: FULL has the blood (on the blasts, red in the hole, a pool under him); CLEAN is the same without any red; OFF cuts the middle away: from the first blast the screen goes black and only the sounds play, then he lies there whole for his two lines. FLASHES and SHAKE in the settings are followed. In the training the ADMIN box has a FINISHER button for the enemy Ryu.

t: CHAPTER 5: YUJI AGAINST IRON MAN IN BLACK FLASH MODE (WITH ALL OF HIS MOVES)
n: You asked for a battle in chapter 5 after Iron Man lands: Yuji in Black Flash mode against Iron Man, with Iron Man on the left and Yuji on the right. It is in the game now. In the huge room of Stark Tower, after the second tap (the dodge, or the punch that throws Yuji into the wall), Tony lands, the screen goes black and the fight begins. The two cards that used to end the chapter (END OF CHAPTER 5 and TO BE CONTINUED) are not shown any more.

THE PICTURE IS TURNED OVER: Iron Man is on the left and Yuji on the right. The LEFT key (or the stick pushed to the left) walks Yuji to the left, towards Iron Man, and the RIGHT key walks him away from him. The health bars, the names and the hit counter changed sides too: Iron Man's are on the left, Yuji's on the right.

YUJI IN BLACK FLASH MODE, as in chapter 4's fight against Meguna: he can walk, jump, dash, block and crouch, and he has ONE attack, the BLACK FLASH on the ATTACK button (it says FLASH): standing it is the punch, in the air the kick to the head, crouched the blow to the stomach. A RING appears on Iron Man where he is going the moment you press. If the fist lands while he is still in the ring it is a perfect Black Flash (half of the normal damage, as for all of Yuji's damage: 30 with the punch, 26 with the kick, 28 with the blow to the stomach). If he has moved off the ring, or he was reeling from a blow, it is WEAK: a quarter of that, and it barely moves him. MODE, BLUE, ULTIMATE and FATAL are not there.

IRON MAN HAS EVERY MOVE YOU CAN DO WHEN YOU PLAY HIM. The ones he already had: R.HOOK, L.HOOK, R.KICK, PUNCH, the ROCKET UPPERCUT, the LOW JABS and the two repulsor bolts. New as the enemy's: the DOWNSLAM (he rises, dives and drives both fists down), the CHARGE (the flying punch of chapter 5: 14 damage and you are knocked down), the BACKFLIP (he turns over backwards away from you), the repulsor BLAST (a beam of blue light for 1.5 seconds that hurts you as long as you stand in front of it: crouching or jumping lets it pass, a guard stops it), the red LASER (a beam 2 pixels thick for 1 second: a guard does not stop it, 20 damage, a stun, and you bleed afterwards), the SPIN BLAST (he turns in a T pose with a beam from each hand: you are hurt while the beam on your side reaches you), the GROUND PUNCH (the road cracks towards you and a shock wave throws you off balance; a jump passes over it) and the BEAR HUG (he charges, grabs you, squeezes three times, carries you up and slams you down for 30).

THE UNIBEAM only when he FEELS THREATENED: his health is below 60%, or he has lost 22% of it in 7 seconds, or two perfect Black Flashes hit him in 10 seconds. Until then he fights with the rest, and he does not use it in the first 15 seconds. All the new moves are in the fights against Iron Man in TRAINING and BATTLE too (grade 1 and up: the downslam, the charge and the blast; 2: the backflip, the ground punch and the bear hug; 3: the spin blast and the laser) and in the ADMIN box of Training.

NOTHING HAPPENS AT THE END, for now, as you said: nobody's health goes below 1, there is no round, no timer and no result screen. The pause screen's MENU leaves the fight and goes to the chapter list; the chapter counts as finished from the moment the fight begins. The hall is 60 metres wide with a wall at each end (1 m = 10 pixels).

TWO DIFFERENCES FROM THE PLAYER'S VERSIONS: the enemy's bear hug does not turn over with you in mid-air (you are carried up and slammed down without the half turn being drawn), and his ground punch is always the street's one (the cracks and the shock wave), never the skyscraper's broken floor.

THE IN-GAME SCAN has a new section, CH 5 FIGHT (59 checks: the start, the skills, left and right, the ring, a perfect and a weak Black Flash, the threat rule, the UNIBEAM only when threatened, nobody can lose, the walls, each of the eight moves started and played to its end, the brain using them all, the ADMIN box, leaving, and the way into the fight from chapter 5 after both taps).

t: ACHIEVEMENTS: THREE TO EARN, AND A RECTANGLE THAT SLIDES IN WHEN YOU DO
n: You asked for an ACHIEVEMENTS button next to the story button. The mode screen (CHOOSE A MODE) has a fourth card now, ACHIEVEMENTS, with a little trophy and how many you have earned (0 OF 3). It opens a screen with one card for each achievement: its picture, its name and what to do. Until you earn it the picture is dark and the card says LOCKED; once you have it the card is gold and says EARNED. BACK (or the Android back button) goes back to the mode screen.

WHEN YOU EARN ONE a rectangle with its picture and its name slides in over the top of the screen, stays for three and a half seconds and slides out again. If two are earned at once the second one waits for the first. Achievements are saved on your device with your money and skills, so they stay earned after you close the game.

JUST THIS ONCE (the picture is Ryu firing a GRANITE BLAST): clash against Ryu at least twice in the same game. A game is one fight: from pressing START until you leave it (a whole Training session, or a whole Battle with all its rounds; REMATCH starts a new one). Only clashes where YOU are Iron Man and the enemy is Ryu count, and a clash counts when its scene is over, whether you won the mash or lost it; leaving the fight in the middle of a clash does not count.

WANNA SEE SOMETHING COOL? (the picture is Sukuna's FUGA): finish an enemy off with Sukuna's FUGA while his domain is active. The arrow itself has to take the last of his health (FUGA takes 40% of the enemy's full health, so he has to be at 40% or less when it lands); a K.O. from the burning after the arrow does not count. FUGA only exists with the domain open and with the FUGA skill, and it cannot kill an enemy with infinite health.

CLIP THIS JARVIS (the picture is the UNIBEAM across a floor of the skyscraper): activate UNIBEAM and throw the enemy off the skyscraper map. To make that possible the UNIBEAM changed a little in the skyscraper: its last burst used to break the floor under the enemy, so he dropped three floors and never went toward a window, even when the window was almost broken. Now, if the enemy stands within 15 m (150 px) of the end of the floor that the beam is going toward, that window shatters and the last burst throws him out of the building, down to the street, instead (you jump out after him). Anywhere else the last burst is exactly as before. The achievement is given when the enemy goes out through a window within 4 seconds of one of your UNIBEAM bursts hitting him.
The three pictures were taken from the game itself. The in-game scan has a new section (ACHIEVEMENTS) and the MENUS part of it looks at the new screen.

t: BEAM CLASH: IRON MAN'S UNIBEAM AGAINST RYU'S JUST THIS ONCE
n: You asked for a beam clash: when a beam fires and another beam is fired, the two meet, a scene plays, you mash buttons for 7 seconds, and the winner overpowers the other one. It works between Iron Man and Ryu, with either of them as your fighter (Iron Man is an enemy since the last update), and only between their two ULTIMATES: Iron Man's UNIBEAM and Ryu's JUST THIS ONCE.

WHEN: the second of the two ultimates starts while the first one is still going on (from its start until its beam is over). Press your ultimate while the enemy's is charging or firing, or the enemy starts his while yours is. Both ultimates are over then (their buttons wait 30 seconds as always) and the clash takes the whole screen. It does not happen in the Wi-Fi fight, in a mirror match (Iron Man against Iron Man, Ryu against Ryu), or when the enemy is on another floor of the skyscraper.

IF IRON MAN FIRED FIRST: he is charging, the sun in his chest swells and the ground shakes, Ryu points at him, the four letters of 今回だけ (JUST THIS ONCE in Japanese) pop up one after the other, and both fire at the same moment. IF RYU FIRED FIRST: Ryu points and fires, his beam hits Iron Man, who braces; then the camera goes to Iron Man, the sun swells, he fires his own beam, and it pushes Ryu's back from his chest to the middle.

THE MASH: the two beams meet in a ball of light and push slowly against each other for 7 seconds. TAP THE SCREEN (or press any key) as fast as you can: the ball moves with the taps and a bar at the top shows who leads. The enemy taps too, about 5 to 8 times a second depending on his grade. The one with more taps wins; a tie is the enemy's.

IRON MAN WINS: his beam overpowers Ryu's, which shrinks to his hair; Ryu steps back and fires a GRANITE BLAST, Iron Man's beam destroys it almost at once and engulfs him. RYU WINS: his beam overpowers Iron Man's; Iron Man flies up on his boots and fires two repulsor beams, the ball gives a little, but in an instant Ryu leaps and DOWNSLAMS him down into the beam.

A FINISHER is a win that would kill the loser: the winning beam takes 45% of the loser's whole health, so if the loser has that much or less left, he is DISINTEGRATED (nothing is left of him and the round is over). Otherwise he takes the 45%, is launched back (Ryu) or sent back (Iron Man) and is stunned for a moment. The winner loses nothing. A health that never runs out (the TRAIN page, or SETTINGS) is never finished.

THE TESTS: the scan of the game has a new part, BEAM CLASH: it starts the clash from the real ultimates in all eight ways (Iron Man or Ryu yours, who fires first, who wins, finisher or not), counts a key as a tap, checks that the loser loses exactly 45% or dies, that the buttons come back, and that it works in the skyscraper too. Eleven deliberate breakages of the code were all caught.

t: IRON MAN CAN BE THE ENEMY NOW
n: You asked for a beam clash between Iron Man and Ryu. For that both of them have to be able to fight each other, and until now Iron Man could only be YOUR fighter in Training. So this update comes first: Iron Man is an ENEMY now. The beam clash itself comes next.

WHERE: on the fighter screen pick him on the enemy side, in Training and in Battle (as your own fighter he is still Training only). SETTINGS > TRAIN > ENEMY IS has him too, and the ADMIN box of the Training lists his moves, so you can make him do any of them at once.

WHAT HE DOES: his chain of four blows (R.HOOK, L.HOOK, R.KICK, PUNCH), the ROCKET UPPERCUT that throws you up, LOW JABS when you are crouched, and repulsor bolts from far away (R.BLAST and L.BLAST). His ULTIMATE is the UNIBEAM: a long charge (2.4 seconds: the ground shakes and light is drawn into his chest), a short brace, then a beam of orange, yellow and white light out of his chest, 12 bursts, one every 0.15 seconds. Nothing stops it, not a guard, a dash, a jump or a crouch: the only way out is to get BEHIND him. Each burst takes 3% of your health (more on the higher grades) and the last one throws you back. A blow on him before it fires ends it. He may start it from Grade 2 up, never in the first 15 seconds of a fight, and then at most every 32 seconds.

WHAT HE CANNOT DO YET: his downslam, charge, backflip, bear hug, laser, spin blast and repulsor beam stay your moves for now. Gojo's and Yuji's FATALITY work on him, he is knocked out like the others, and in a mirror match he has the inverted colours.

THE TESTS: the scan of the game now plays him as an enemy in free play and in a Battle against Ryu, checks his list in the ADMIN box, plays every move of that list, his UNIBEAM from start to end and the fatalities of Gojo and Yuji on him.

t: THE CAMERA CAN NO LONGER FREEZE AFTER A MISSING PICTURE
n: You sent an error report: Uncaught TypeError, cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'width'), and said you were using the menu and your camera glitched and got messed up. I looked at it. The error came from the part of the game that draws the pictures of the fighters (the part that adds the trails and the shadows when those graphics options are on): it was asked to draw a picture that did not exist, in the middle of drawing a fighter.

WHY THE CAMERA BROKE: to draw a fighter the game cuts a window the size of his picture out of the screen, draws him inside it and takes the window away again. The error stopped the drawing in the middle, so the window was never taken away: from then on only that small window was redrawn, and the rest of the picture froze or sat in the wrong place. I made it happen on purpose in a test: one missing picture left the screen broken for good, until the fight was started again.

WHAT I CHANGED: a picture that does not exist is now skipped for that one moment, and written down in SETTINGS > ERRORS as A PICTURE WAS MISSING AND WAS SKIPPED, with the place in the game where it was asked for. Your own fighter shows the last picture of his move instead of a missing one. And if a picture goes wrong in some other way, the game now puts the screen back exactly as it was before it goes on, so one error can no longer leave the camera broken. The error is still written down.

THE ERROR REPORT is better: every error now also says what the game was doing when it came: the screen, who was fighting whom, training or battle, street or skyscraper, whether your fighter was swinging, hurt or in cursed energy mode, and the speed setting. With that I can find out which picture it was.

WHAT I COULD NOT FIND: I played about 160 random fights with your exact settings (trails, shadows, glow, TURBO, unlimited frame rate, the fixed retro size) with every fighter on both maps, with the admin box, and with the options changed in the middle of a fight, and the missing picture never came up. So I know why the camera broke and I made sure it cannot break again, but I do not know yet which move it was. If it happens again, send me the report: it will name the place now. If you remember which fighter and which move you were using, tell me.

t: TRAINING: AN ADMIN BOX WITH EVERY MOVE OF THE ENEMY, ONE TAP AND HE DOES IT
n: You asked for a button at the top of the training that opens an admin panel with the moves of the enemy, as a small box on the top of the screen that scrolls, so it does not take up the whole screen. It is there. In the training, in a room with an enemy who fights, the top bar has a new ADMIN button next to SET. Tap it and a small box opens at the top, about a third of the screen high, and it starts after the top bar, so it never covers a button. Tap ADMIN again or the X in the box to close it. The box hides during a cutscene and under the PAUSE and SETTINGS screens, and the DAMAGE METER and the MOVE INFO of the TRAIN page move down under it while it is open. A Battle has no ADMIN button.

THE MOVES TAB: the box has two tabs, and the first one is a list of every move the enemy has, one button each. You said a tap should make him do the move once, right now, and that is what it does: the enemy starts that move the way his own brain starts it in a fight, so it looks the same, takes the same time and hits for the same damage. The list scrolls up and down with a finger or the mouse wheel. Gojo: R.HOOK, L.HOOK, ELBOW, KICK. Yuji: his 15 blows, POWER UP and POWER OFF. Verity: the 4 blows, BITE, LOW CLAW. The Cat: GRAB, PUNCH, GRAB 2, KICK, SMASH, PUSH DASH, CARTOON. Freddy: R.SLASH, L.SLASH, the two FAR punches, BOILING WATER, PIERCE, GROUND SLAM. Sukuna: his 12 blows, AIR CUT, FIRE ARROW. Ryu: his 12 blows and KI BLAST. Every enemy also has BLOCK and DODGE.

THE ORANGE BUTTONS are the big ones: the FINISHER (his fatality on you: Gojo, Verity, the Cat and Freddy have one), the Cat's ULTIMATE, Verity's JUMPSCARE, Freddy's NIGHTMARE, Sukuna's SHRINE and Ryu's JUST ONCE. They play to the end like in a fight, and the training goes on afterwards: when the FINISHER ends the round for you, the next round starts by itself. A move only starts when the fight is on, he stands on the ground and no cutscene is running. If it cannot, the box says WAIT, BUSY or K.O. over you. NOT NOW means that move needs you standing on the ground: the JUMPSCARE, the ULTIMATE and the NIGHTMARE do not work while you jump, dash, crouch or are hurt.

FREEZE: the button in the top of the box. While the box is open and it says FREEZE: ON (it does when you open it), the enemy's own brain stands still: he does not walk, attack, block or dodge by himself, so only the move you tapped happens and nothing follows it (his chain of blows, a power-up of his own, a defence against your swing). Tap it to get FREEZE: OFF and he fights back again with the behaviour you chose in SETTINGS > TRAIN, even with the box open. With the box closed the behaviour of the room is back whatever FREEZE says. The box does not walk him up to you: a blow reaches only as far as it does in a fight. Yuji's shortest blows (R.HOOK, L.HOOK, KNEE) reach about 2.3 metres (23 pixels), a little less than CLOSE, so step up to him if you want them to hit.

THE TOOLS TAB: HEAL gives him his full health, and starts a new round if he was knocked out. INF HP keeps him at full health (the same as ENEMY HEALTH: INFINITE in SETTINGS > TRAIN). CLOSE, MID and FAR put him 2.8, 7 or 13 metres (28, 70 and 130 pixels) in front of you, one tap each. ENEMY switches to the next enemy (Gojo, Yuji, Verity, Cat, Freddy, Sukuna, Ryu) without leaving the room, and the list of moves changes with him.

SMALL THINGS: Yuji's R.KICK, ELBOW, DOWNSLAM and PUSH KICK are blows of his cursed energy mode, so the flames come on for the blow and go off after it (unless you pressed POWER UP first). A knocked-down enemy gets up when you tap a move. Tapping a button never leaves the keyboard on it, so SPACE and ENTER still play the game.

t: RYU: ALL HIS PICTURES REDRAWN TURNED OVER, HIS BLOWS SWING AT THE ENEMY
n: You said his hand was punching the air, and told me to change the WHAT YOU WILL SEE part and to turn all of his pictures to the side of the updated image. You were right: in version 1.204 I only flipped the old pictures, so his face looked at the enemy but his arms and legs swung to the other side. This time I rebuilt his whole picture set from his drawing turned over, so he looks like the updated image and every blow swings at the enemy. I also changed the WHAT YOU WILL SEE part of the 1.204 entry, which was wrong.

WHAT CHANGED: all 40 sets of pictures are redrawn: standing, walking, walking back, jumping, crouching, blocking, dashing, getting hurt, getting knocked out, the 5-hit combo and every punch and kick. The GRANITE BLAST mode and JUST THIS ONCE kept the old side in 1.204; they are turned too now, so his hair cannon points at the enemy, the beam leaves the tip of his hair, and he no longer turns to the other side when he fires them. His character card, his face picture, the map and VS screens and an enemy Ryu are the same, and an enemy Ryu turns round when you stand behind him, like every fighter.

WHAT YOU WILL SEE: his face, his chest and his long front leg point at the enemy, and his guard (the arm held in front of his face) is on his back side, as in the updated image. His fists and his elbow cross his body and come out at the enemy, and his kicks go out with his front leg: nothing punches the air behind him any more.

THE FIST TOUCHES THE ENEMY: turned over, his long front leg reaches further than his fists, and the game counted that foot as part of every punch. He stopped when his foot touched the enemy and his fist stayed 1 to 2.5 metres (10 to 25 pixels) short of him, which is a punch at the air again. A punch is now counted by its arm only, so the fist is what touches the enemy where the hit lands, and a kick is counted by the kicking leg only. His hooks, hard punch, uppercut and elbow reach a little less far from his body than before, so he steps in a little further for them, and the farthest enemy each blow still reaches is the same as in 1.204.

THE NUMBERS: his body, his reach and the place where each of his blows lands are measured again on the new pictures, so what you see is what hits. The same 27 test blows as before, the 7 blasts and the dive punch (at 3 to 5 distances each) still hit and do exactly the same damage as in 1.204. One difference: his guard is now behind him, so his chest is about 1.5 metres (15 pixels) less far forward than it was. An enemy has to come that much closer to touch him, and he can stand that much closer to an enemy (the distance at which two fighters push each other apart is smaller).

t: RYU: HIS PICTURE IS TURNED OVER SO HE FACES THE ENEMY
n: You asked me to mirror Ryu's sprite because he was turning to the wrong side. You answered my questions: you wanted only his picture turned over, so that he faces right, with the hits still landing on his right, where he is facing, and of the two test pictures the turned-over one was the one that faces the enemy. Here it is.

WHAT CHANGED: every picture of Ryu is turned over: standing, walking, jumping, crouching, blocking, dashing, every punch and kick, getting hurt and getting knocked out. It is the same on his character card, his face picture, the map screen and the VS screen. When Ryu is your enemy he faces you the right way round as well, and when you stand behind him he turns to the other side, like every fighter.

NOTHING ELSE MOVED: his body, his reach and the place where each of his blows lands are measured on the old pictures, so they are exactly what they were (the same 27 test blows at three distances do the same damage as in V1.202). His body stays exactly where it was on the screen too, so that an enemy's blow touches him where you see him and does not hit the air in front of his chest.

WHAT YOU WILL SEE: his face now looked at the enemy, but the picture was only flipped, so his arms and legs swung to the other side and his punches went at the air behind him, while the hit still landed on his right. That was wrong, and version 1.205 fixes it: all of his pictures are redrawn turned over, so every blow swings towards the enemy (see 1.205).

t: IRON MAN: ULTIMATE, THE UNIBEAM FIRED FROM HIS CHEST
n: You asked for Iron Man's ultimate: he charges up from the core in his chest, braces, and fires a mix of orange, yellow and white beam from his chest. No questions this time, so here it is. The DOMAIN button (key V) was hidden for him until now; it is now his ULTIMATE (the button says ULTIMATE and is orange). It costs 67 percent of your energy and needs 30 seconds to come back, like the ultimates of Ryu and Sukuna.

HOW IT PLAYS: CHARGE (2.4 seconds): he lets his guard go, pushes his chest forward, and the arc reactor in it swells from a spark into a sun of orange, yellow and white light, with sparks and rings pulled into it and the ground shaking more and more. BRACE (half a second): his feet go wide apart, his hips go down and he leans back against what is coming. FIRE (1.8 seconds): a huge beam of orange, yellow and white light, 4 m thick, leaves the middle of his chest and crosses the whole screen, with a warm flash, dust behind him and the screen shaking. RELEASE: the beam thins and goes out and he stands up.

THE DAMAGE: nothing can touch him from the moment you press the button until it is over, and nothing can stop the beam: not blocking, not dashing, not jumping, not lying on the floor. The one enemy it misses is one who has gone BEHIND him. 12 bursts take 45 percent of the enemy's whole health in all (as much as the other ultimates), push him back along the beam and stun him, and the last burst throws him away. A smoke ball is immune. In the skyscraper the beam breaks the furniture, walls and doors in its way, the lights shake, and the last burst breaks 3 floors under the enemy.

THE REST: the beam is 4 m thick (1 metre = 10 pixels, as you said). The charge, the brace, the beam and its bursts have new sounds, the fighter card now lists UNIBEAM, and the ULTIMATE button of the other fighters is not affected.

t: IRON MAN: SPIN BLAST, A SPINNING T POSE WITH A BEAM FROM EACH HAND
n: You asked for a new move for Iron Man: when you jump and use the blast special, he spins in a T pose and fires a beam from each hand. No questions this time, so here it is: turn the REPULSOR mode on (MODE), jump, and press the BLUE button in the air (it says SPIN BLAST there). He hangs just above the floor with his arms straight out and his boots blazing, turns on the spot and both palms fire at once, one beam to each side, for 1.7 seconds.

HOW THE BEAMS BEHAVE: they are the arms of the T, so seen from the side an arm that points across the screen is long and one that points at you or away from you is short. The beams breathe in and out, twice every turn, left and right together. An enemy close to him is hit most of the time, one far away only while the beams are at their longest. 16 hits of 3 damage at most (a crouching enemy is flown over, a blocker only sparks, one hit for the combo counter), and in the skyscraper both beams cut the furniture, walls and doors in their way.

HE HOVERS LOW ON PURPOSE: a T pose at the height of a jump would fire over the head of a standing enemy, so he sinks to 0.6 m above the floor and the beams pass at the head and neck of the enemy. A blow that lands on him stops the move and he falls; it shares the 10 second wait of the BLAST (3 seconds if he is hit before the beams are out). Pressed on the ground, BLUE is still the BLAST.

1 METRE = 10 PIXELS: you said a meter in real life is 10 pixels, so every number of the new move is in metres (the hover is 0.6 m, the reach 25 m) and every new number from now on will be. The moves and pictures that already exist were not resized (Iron Man himself is about 6 m tall on this scale).

t: BLEEDS, BURNS AND OTHER TICK DAMAGE NO LONGER STACK
n: You asked that anything that deals tick damage (a bleed, a poison or whatever) cannot stack: it deals a consistent amount until it is over, and it starts again if the enemy is hit after it has faded. You answered two questions about it: a second hit while it is still running does nothing (it keeps its old timer and its damage), and only ONE tick effect can run on a fighter at a time, so a bleed also blocks a burn and the other way round. There is no poison in the game, so this covers every bleed, burn and scald.

IT IS THE SAME FOR EVERYTHING AND FOR BOTH SIDES: Verity's bites, Yuji's Piercing Blood and Cleave, Freddy's claw, boiling water and Nightmare, Sukuna's cuts and fire arrows, Iron Man's laser, and what the enemies do to you. The blow itself still lands with all its damage, only the extra bleed or burn is ignored while one is running. A bleed or burn that has faded starts again with the next blow that brings one.

SUKUNA: the Cut Storm, the Dash Slash and Dismantle used to add one more bleed for every cut that landed, so the bleeds piled up and took a lot of health in a few seconds. Now they start ONE bleed (4 seconds, 8 seconds for Dismantle and 6 for the Dash Slash) and the other cuts of the same move add nothing. The BLEED x3 words are gone.
LOST LIMBS (GRAPHIC DAMAGE FULL): the bleeding of a limb that was ripped off takes the same amount whether one limb is gone or three, and it waits while a bleed or a burn is running.

NOT IN THIS: what the big moves do over time is the move itself, not something left on the enemy: the shrine's cuts, the jumpscare's fear and the beam of the blast. Say so if they should follow the same rule.

t: NO STREET BUTTON: THE WAY OUT IS THE FRONT DOOR, AND IT IS EASY TO FIND
n: You asked for a door to leave the building instead of the STREET button, so the button is gone from the elevator panel (TOP, LOBBY, ENEMY and LAST are all that is left). The way out is the front door at the far left end of the lobby: walk into it and you are in the street, with the skyscraper standing behind you. You chose to keep only that one door and to make it easy to find.
THE FRONT DOOR IS HARD TO MISS NOW: a big sign across its glass says EXIT, with STREET under it, and EXIT blinks. The cold light of the street spills into the lobby around the door.

THE SIGNS ALL OVER THE LOBBY POINT TO IT: the wall signs of the lobby used to say FLOOR 1, now they say an arrow and EXIT, with the 1 still under it. The arrow points left, to the door, and it blinks one sign after the other in that direction, so you can follow them from the elevator. The stairs door of the lobby says STAIRS now, so EXIT only means the street.

t: THE CITY, PART 2: A STREET BUTTON IN THE ELEVATOR, DOOR SOUNDS, THE BUILDING IN CUTSCENES
n: You said "continue" after I offered three things for the connected maps, so all three are in.

A STREET BUTTON in the elevator panel (the fifth quick button, next to TOP, LOBBY, ENEMY and LAST): press it in the cab and the cab rides down to the lobby, its doors open, and a moment later you step out and go straight out through the front door into the street. It saves the long walk from the elevator to the front door. If the cab is already at the lobby you go out at once. Pressing any other button cancels the trip, and a jammed lobby door says OUT OF ORDER as always. The enemy follows out of the front door a moment later as usual.

DOOR SOUNDS: the glass doors of the front door make a soft sliding whoosh and a two-note chime when they take you and when the enemy comes through; when you step out into the street you hear a wash of traffic (a rumble, a car going past, a far horn) and when you step into the lobby the street goes quiet behind you.

THE BUILDING IN CUTSCENES: the front of the skyscraper in the street no longer vanishes when a fatality or another cutscene of a fight starts: it is drawn over the same street, so the picture does not change.

t: THE MAPS ARE CONNECTED: LEAVE THE SKYSCRAPER BY ITS FRONT DOOR AND YOU ARE IN THE STREET
n: You said: connect the maps together, the street is on floor one: if you leave the building through the front door you go right into the street map. You answered one round of questions: you walk into the door (no button), the enemy follows a moment later, the maps are joined both ways and the map screen keeps both buttons, and you wanted two extras: windows that lead to the street, and the street seen in the lobby's windows.

THE FRONT DOOR: the lobby (floor 1) of the skyscraper has a glass front door at its left end, with a lit STREET sign. Walk into it (hold the direction towards it for a moment) and you are in the street, standing in front of the building. In the street the building stands a little to the left of where a fight begins: a tower with a lit lobby, a TOWER sign over glass doors that slide apart when you come near. Walk into those doors and you are in the lobby again. A door only takes you if you walk INTO it: stand in it and walk away and nothing happens, and after you have used a door you must let go of the key (or walk 60 pixels away) before it takes you again.

THE ENEMY FOLLOWS A MOMENT LATER: when you go out he comes out of the front door about a second after you; if he was on a higher floor he has to come down (about 1.4 seconds plus 0.4 seconds a floor, at most 8 seconds) and the screen says FOE 12 DOWN. When you go in he follows through the lobby's front door (the screen says FOE OUTSIDE until he is in). PUT ENEMY and RESET of free play bring him to where you are, in the street too.

THE MAP SCREEN stays as it is: it says where the match STARTS, the street or the penthouse (floor 50). Every round of a match begins where the match began. The building keeps everything while you are out in the street: broken walls, craters, wrecks, the elevator.

WINDOWS LEAD TO THE STREET: a fighter thrown through the glass at the end of any floor falls all the way down into the street map. If you are thrown out the camera falls with you, floor after floor, to the street (3% of your health a floor, at most 30%, never a K.O., as before), you land in front of the building and the enemy comes down after you a moment later. If the enemy is thrown out you jump out after him (DOWN TO THE STREET). The glass of the lobby lets you out into the street too.
THE LOBBY'S WINDOWS SHOW THE STREET: the shops and the lamps of the street map, and cars driving past with their lights on, instead of the sky.
It is there in Free Play and Battle, on both maps. Not in the story fights, the hunts, the rush, the curses and Wi-Fi.

t: IRON MAN: THE ATTACK IS CALLED LASER, AND IT IS 2 PIXELS THICK
n: You said: the attack is called laser, not red laser, and it is 2 pixels thick.
It is called LASER now: on the BLUE button (when the REPULSOR mode is on and you are walking back), in the button's spoken description and in the move's notes. The beam itself is still red.

The beam is exactly 2 pixels thick now: two rows of light, a bright almost white row on top of a red one, with streaks of light running along it, from his palm to the edge of the screen. The part that hurts is the same 2 rows (it was 3 rows, and with the glow around it it was drawn 5 to 11 pixels thick). The flares at his palm and where the laser goes into the enemy and comes out of him are smaller to match, so nothing on screen is thicker than the line.

Everything else is as in 1.196: it cuts through anything, a guard does not stop it, it pierces the enemy for 20 damage, he is stunned and does not bleed while the laser is through him, then he bleeds and stays stunned. 12 second cooldown (shared with the blast).

t: IRON MAN: GROUND PUNCH (CROUCH) AND RED LASER (WALK BACK IN THE REPULSOR MODE)
n: You said: if I crouch and use the move (the bear hug) I punch the ground, and in the skyscraper, while the enemy and I are falling, I punch his face and send him back; on the street I punch the ground, crack it and make the enemy unstable. And if I walk back and use blast I fire a concentrated red laser that cuts through anything for 1 second: it pierces the enemy, who is stunned but does not bleed while the laser is through him because all his blood is vaporized, and after that he starts to bleed and stays stunned for a few seconds.

The BLUE button has four forms now and its name tells you which one you get: BEAR HUG when you stand, GROUND PUNCH while you are crouched, BLAST when the REPULSOR mode is on, and RED LASER when the REPULSOR mode is on and you are walking back (holding the back direction).

GROUND PUNCH: from the crouch he raises his right fist high over his head and slams it into the ground. On the STREET the road cracks towards the enemy and the shock runs along the ground; when it reaches him (up to 200 px away) he is thrown off balance: 8 damage, flung up and stunned for 1.2 seconds. A guard does not stop it and a crouching enemy is not spared, but an enemy who jumps over it is not touched. In the SKYSCRAPER the floor breaks under both of you and you fall two floors together (one from the 2nd floor); while you fall Iron Man punches the enemy in the face, 14 damage, and sends him flying back. You land, the enemy on his back. Each of you loses 3% of health a floor from the fall, never enough to K.O. In the lobby it is the street version, and it does nothing when the enemy is on another floor. 10 second cooldown (shared with the bear hug).

RED LASER: he braces his raised arm with both hands, a ring of red light closes on his palm (about 0.6 seconds) and a thin, concentrated red laser fires across the screen for exactly 1 second. It cuts through anything: a guard does not stop it, and in the SKYSCRAPER the furniture, walls and doors in its way are cut at once. An enemy it touches is pierced: 20 damage and a hole through him. For as long as the laser is through him he is stunned, steams and does NOT bleed, because all his blood is vaporized, and it does 1 more damage every 0.1 seconds. When the laser is gone the hole opens: he starts to BLEED (2 damage every half second for 4 seconds, with blood when GRAPHIC DAMAGE is on FULL) and stays stunned for 3 more seconds. A crouching or dodging enemy is not touched. 12 second cooldown (shared with the blast).

A blow that lands on him before the fist hits the ground, or while the laser is charging or firing, stops the move (a laser that had already pierced the enemy still starts him bleeding). He is still in TRAINING only.

t: IRON MAN: BLAST (A CHARGED BEAM FROM HIS PALM, CONTINUOUS DAMAGE)
n: You said: in the repulsor mode make the bear hug change into Blast: Iron Man lifts his arm forward, charges a beam in his palm and then fires a beam forward that deals continuous damage.

The BLUE button is the same special in two forms: BEAR HUG as usual, and BLAST while the REPULSOR mode (the MODE button) is on. The button changes its name by itself when you switch the mode, and the bear hug is exactly as it was.

Press BLAST: he lifts his right arm straight out in front of him with his feet braced, a ball of light grows in his palm while sparks are drawn into it (about 0.7 seconds), and then a beam fires forward to the edge of the screen for about 1.2 seconds. While the beam touches the enemy it burns him every 0.1 seconds for 3 damage (45 in all) and holds him in place. The combo counter counts it as one hit whose damage keeps growing.

The beam is at the height of his palm: an enemy who crouches is flown over, and one beyond the edge of the screen is out of reach. A blocking enemy takes nothing, the beam only sparks on his guard. In the SKYSCRAPER the beam also breaks the furniture, walls and doors in its way.
A blow that lands on him before or while the beam is out stops it. It has a 10 second cooldown (3 seconds if it was stopped before it fired). He is still in TRAINING only.

t: IRON MAN: BEAR HUG (CHARGE GRAB, FLY UP THROUGH THE FLOORS, TURN, DIVE DOWN)
n: You said: add a charge grab move to his base through his special, and when he grabs the enemy he bear hugs them, then flies up breaking the floors above, then goes 180 and flies down much faster breaking the floors below.

His special is the BLUE button (key L), and it says BEAR HUG now. Press it and he opens his arms and charges at the enemy: fast, 150 px at the most. If his arms touch the enemy he grabs him and pulls him in, and the bear hug squeezes three times, 3 damage each, that cannot be blocked. A charge that touches nothing skids to a stop (you can try again after 3 seconds); a grab has a 12 second cooldown. It works in the base form and in the REPULSOR mode.

Then he flies up with the enemy in his arms. In the SKYSCRAPER the ceilings above them break, 3 floors (fewer near the top: there is nothing above floor 50), and the camera rises with the two of them. On the street they fly up to the top of the screen.

At the top the two of them turn over 180 degrees and he dives head first, about twice as fast as he climbed. In the skyscraper the floor he took off from and the 2 below it break, and they fall through every hole, the new ones and the ones of the climb, up to 6 floors, and he slams the enemy into the floor: 22 damage plus 5 for every floor they fell. On the street the slam is 30 damage. The enemy is knocked down.
The enemy has to be on his floor, and not in the air, crouching, dodging or already down, for the grab to work. He is still in TRAINING only.

t: IRON MAN: REPULSOR MODE (BLASTS FROM HIS RIGHT AND LEFT HAND)
n: You said: add a repulsor mode to Iron Man that makes his M1s blasts from his right hand, and the second one from his left hand, that's it for now.

The MODE button (key E) is back for Iron Man and switches the REPULSOR mode on and off: it lights up and says MODE REPULSOR while the mode is on. In the mode, pressing ATTACK on the ground fires a blast from his right hand (R.BLAST, 6 damage), the next press a blast from his left hand (L.BLAST, 7 damage), then the right hand again, and so on. The ATTACK button says which hand is next.

A blast: his arm comes up and points at the enemy with the palm flashing, and a bolt of light leaves the palm and flies at the enemy fast (about 420 px a second, 1.2 seconds at the most) until it touches him. A blocking enemy blocks it, and an enemy who is crouching is flown over.

Everything else is as it was, in the mode too: crouch + ATTACK is still the low jabs, dash + ATTACK the charge, JUMP + ATTACK the rocket uppercut, ATTACK in the air the downslam, and DASH back twice the backflip. Switch the mode off and the 4-hit combo is back. The mode switches itself off when a new fight starts.
Both blasts stay at 15 damage or less, the M1 rule. He is still in TRAINING only.

t: IRON MAN: LOW JABS, CHARGE PUNCH AND THRUSTER BACKFLIP
n: You said: if I crouch and punch he does 2 lower punches, if I dash and punch it is the punch Iron Man almost did on Yuji at the end of chapter 5, and if I double dash back he does a backflip using the thrusters in his legs.

LOW JABS: crouch (S or the stick down) and press ATTACK. He throws two quick low punches, right and left (5 and 6 damage), that also reach an enemy who is crouching. Press ATTACK again during them and two more follow. The button says LOW JABS while you are crouched.

CHARGE: dash, then press ATTACK (during the dash or up to about 0.4 seconds after it began; DASH and ATTACK together work too). He crouches back with the fist drawn, lights his boots and flies at the enemy lying flat on his side with the fist straight out, flames and speed lines behind him, like the punch of chapter 5. The first time the fist touches the enemy it lands (14 damage, the enemy is thrown about 140 px and knocked down) or is blocked, and Iron Man stops there. A charge that touches nothing flies up to 150 px and lands. The button says CHARGE during a dash.

BACKFLIP: press DASH twice quickly going back (the second press within 0.5 seconds of the first, without holding forward). His boots burst, he rises curled up and turns over backwards with the flames lit, and lands about 70 px further back than the first dash took him. The enemy's blows miss while he is high in the air. Two dashes forward are still just two dashes.
All the new blows stay at 15 damage or less, the M1 rule. He is still in TRAINING only, and the BLUE, MODE, DOMAIN, FATAL and SENSE buttons stay hidden.

t: IRON MAN FIGHTS: COMBO, ROCKET UPPERCUT, DOWNSLAM, BLOCK, DASH, CROUCH
n: You said: add attacks for Iron Man: a right hook, then a left hook, then a roundhouse kick, then a punch forward; jump and punch at the same time is an uppercut; jump, wait 0.2 seconds and punch is a downslam. You chose: the uppercut throws the enemy up and the downslam knocks him down, a ROCKET uppercut, and also block + dash, crouch, and hurt + K.O. pictures.

ATTACK: R.HOOK (8 damage), L.HOOK (9), R.KICK (12, the roundhouse kick, at chest height) and PUNCH (8, a lunging straight punch that sends the enemy flying back), one after the other: press ATTACK again within 0.7 seconds, or during a blow (the press is kept), for the next one. All of them stay at 15 damage or less, the M1 rule.

ROCKET UPPERCUT: press JUMP and ATTACK together (within about 0.1 seconds, either one first). He blasts up with his boots lit, the fist rises through the enemy's chin (14 damage) and throws him up in the air.

DOWNSLAM: jump, and from 0.2 seconds after the jump began press ATTACK in the air. He hangs for a moment with both fists overhead, dives onto the enemy (8 damage) and drives him onto the floor. An ATTACK pressed a little before the 0.2 seconds waits until then. The button says DOWNSLAM while you are in the air.

The rest: CROUCH (stick down or S, he kneels), BLOCK (hold the button: a high guard with the palm lit), DASH (a burst of the boots: forward he flies at the enemy with the flames behind him and goes through him, back he hovers away), HURT pictures (he flinches, doubles over or staggers when he is hit) and a K.O. in which he falls on his back. The BLUE, MODE, DOMAIN, FATAL and SENSE buttons stay hidden: he has no powers yet. He is still in TRAINING only.

t: IRON MAN IN TRAINING, AND THE INV. FIGHTER IN INVERTED COLOURS
n: You said: make the INV. fighter have inverted colours, and make the Iron Man sprite from chapter 5 a playable character in TRAINING: you can only see his idle, you can move him, you can't do anything yet. You chose: only the colours for the INV. fighter, walk + jump for Iron Man, nothing else.

THE INV. FIGHTER: pick the same fighter on both sides and the one on the right is the INV. (inverted) one. Gojo, Yuji, Verity, the Cat and Freddy already had inverted colours, but the INV. Sukuna and the INV. Ryu were still drawn in their normal colours on the fighter screen, the map screen and the VS screen. Now they are inverted too. Nothing else about them changed (in the fight their bodies already were inverted).

IRON MAN (TRAINING): the red and gold suit of chapter 5 is the fourth fighter of the top row of the fighter screen (the faces are 4 + 4 now). Pick him as YOUR fighter in TRAINING, on the street or the skyscraper, against any enemy: he stands in his ready stance with the glowing palm, WALKS forwards and backwards and JUMPS with the flames of his boots lit. Keyboard: arrows or A / D to walk, W, Up or Space to jump; on a phone the stick.

He cannot do anything else yet: no attacks, block, dash or crouch, so those buttons are hidden while he fights. The enemy's blows hurt him and a knock-out ends the round as for everyone (he has no hurt or K.O. pictures yet, so he just stands there). In BATTLE his face says TRAIN ONLY, in WI-FI NOT ONLINE, and he cannot be the enemy yet.

t: SUKUNA AND RYU FIGHT IN BATTLE, ON BOTH SIDES
n: You said: make Sukuna in the fighting mode and not just the training mode. You chose: play him AND fight him, and Ryu too. The picker no longer says TRAINING ONLY: Sukuna (still bought for $3000 on the SKILLS page, on both sides) and Ryu can be YOUR fighter in Battle (best of 3 rounds, K.O., results, rematch) and the ENEMY in Battle and in Training. Not in the Wi-Fi fight.

THE ENEMY SUKUNA: R.JAB, L.JAB and FACE KICK up close; from beyond 60 px his M1 throws slashes (R.SLASH, L.SLASH, X SLASH) as when you play him; the AIR CUT (a slash that cuts you and makes you bleed for 2 seconds); from GRADE 2 up the fire arrow (a long cast you can interrupt, then an arrow that burns you for 8 seconds); from SEMI-GRADE 1 up his domain, MALEVOLENT SHRINE (the sign, then 6 seconds of cuts across you, about 3 health every half second, nothing blocks them, a blow of yours ends it).

THE ENEMY RYU: hooks, hard punch, front kick, leg kick, kick up, now and then the POWER PUNCH, the 5-HIT COMBO and the DASH KICK, a ki blast from afar, and from SEMI-GRADE 1 up JUST THIS ONCE: the stance, then a beam that hits you ten times (your guard, jump and dash decide what reaches you). He has his own K.O. pictures.

Their blows are the same data the game plays when you are Sukuna or Ryu (pictures, speed, step and every IMPACT with its damage), so your guard, crouch, jump, dash and the grade damage work on them as on every enemy.

FATALITIES: Gojo's and the Cat's fatality on you as Sukuna or Ryu now show YOU (they showed a Gojo or a Cat), and Gojo's, the Cat's and Yuji's on them as enemies work (Yuji's uses the script made for Freddy, in their colours). Verity's and Freddy's fatality have no version for them yet: the button stays dark against them, and the enemy Verity and Freddy do not do theirs on you as Sukuna or Ryu (Freddy's Nightmare does work).

NOT DONE: the enemy versions of Sukuna's DISMANTLE (time stop), LEG CUT, CUT STORM, DASH SLASH, CLEAVE moves and flame mode, and Ryu's other blasts; they have no fatality of their own as enemies. Bot duels (a bot plays Gojo against them at three grades): the enemy Sukuna hurts it for about 50, 60 and 280 of its 300 health at GRADE 3, SEMI-GRADE 1 and SPECIAL GRADE, the enemy Ryu for about 10, 130 and 275 (Yuji 14 / 134 / 296, the Cat 166 / 291 / 279): they are on the soft side in the middle, tell me if you want them harder.

The game scan now plays matches with Sukuna and Ryu on both sides, three fighters' fatality on them, the enemy fatalities and nightmare on them, and every special move of theirs: 23,254 checks, no errors.

t: FREDDY AS AN ENEMY, AND HIS DAMAGE BALANCED
n: You said: make Freddy an enemy in versus and make his damage balanced. You chose everything: he can fight you with all his moves, put YOU to sleep with his Nightmare and eat you with his Fatality, and Yuji's Fatality gets its own Freddy version. The enemy picker no longer says NOT AS ENEMY for him (in Battle, Training and Wi-Fi), and you need to own him on the SKILLS page like the other fighters.

HOW HE FIGHTS: he walks in, slashes (claw, then bare hand), and from far away stretches his arm like when you play him (left, right, left). He also throws his boiling water (it burns you for 6 seconds), from GRADE 3 up the pierce (nothing blocks it, you bleed) and the ground slam (in the street the road cracks and he throws stones, in the skyscraper the floor breaks under both of you and he throws the furniture), and from SEMI-GRADE 1 up the Nightmare (once in 30 seconds, when you stand within 150 px: you fall asleep, he comes out of the dark in the dream, four slashes, the pierce, and you wake up bleeding) and, at your 20% health, the Fatality: the same leg-eating scene, on whoever you play (it follows GRAPHIC DAMAGE: FULL, CLEAN or OFF). Your guard, crouch, jump and dash decide what reaches you, as with every enemy. He blocks and dodges like the others of his grade.

THE FATALITIES ON HIM: Gojo's, Verity's, the Cat's and his own (a mirror match: the enemy Freddy has the inverted colours) work on him; Verity's showed a Verity as the victim before. Yuji's Fatality has its own Freddy version: another order of blows (elbow, hook, knee, slam, sweep, spin, dive, then the huge one), sparks and pieces in the red and green of his sweater, and the embers of his boiler room rising over the screen. His hurt pictures are used for the reactions of the victim now.

BALANCE: bot duels (a simple bot plays each fighter against each enemy at three grades, 3 to 4 times each). Played by the bot, Freddy finished a fight in about 21 seconds, between Verity (20) and Gojo (26 to 36); his M1 blows are now 85% of what the shared tables say (the stretched punches did 10 and 12), the water is 22 (was 25), the pierce 26 (was 30), and the stones of the slam are 8 (were 6, the move was the weakest per energy). As an enemy he hurts a standing bot for about 15, 170 and 290 of its 300 health at GRADE 3, SEMI-GRADE 1 and SPECIAL GRADE: in the middle of the other four enemies (Gojo 92 / 233 / 45, Yuji 14 / 134 / 296, Verity 79 / 215 / 216, the Cat 166 / 291 / 279).

A BUG FOUND AND FIXED: Freddy's stretched punches were numbers 60 and 61 of the game's tables, and two curse moves had those numbers too: since V1.185 they had Freddy's damage and push instead of their own. His new numbers are 90 and 91, the curses are as they were.
The game scan now plays the Fatality of every fighter on the enemy Freddy, his Nightmare and Fatality on five different fighters, and his three specials: 24,923 checks, no errors.

t: NO HIT COUNTER OR DAMAGE NUMBERS IN CUTSCENES
n: You said: hide the hit counter and damage numbers (I had offered it for the cutscenes, so that is where it applies). In every cutscene the hit counter (the HITS and DMG lines, the BONUS line and the four combo squares) and the floating damage numbers are gone: Freddy's nightmare, Yuji's ultimate and fatality, every fatality, the Cat's choke, Verity's jumpscare, the opening and closing of a domain, Sukuna's FUGA, the blindfold close-ups, and Ryu's JUST THIS ONCE (the whole beam too, although the health bars are back for it).
What a cutscene counted stays hidden after it ends too: the counter does not pop up for the last second of its window. The next hit you land starts it again, as before.
Ordinary fights are unchanged: the counter and the numbers show there as always. The hits of a cutscene still count in the combo and in the damage exactly as before; only the drawing is gone.
A check that lists every text drawn in every cutscene found no HITS, DMG, BONUS or damage number left, and the same check still sees them in normal fights. Game scan: 23,846 checks, no errors.

t: CUTSCENES WITHOUT CAPTIONS
n: You said: remove any text from any cutscene that says what is happening, or that you did not ask for (for example THE DAMAGE IS REAL in Freddy's dream). Every word I had added to a cutscene is gone.
FREDDY'S NIGHTMARE: NIGHTMARE, THE DREAM, THE DAMAGE IS REAL, WAKE UP!, the Z letters over the sleeping enemy and the PIERCED! word at the pierce.

YUJI'S FATALITY: the BLACK FLASH x1 ... x8 counter, the caption lines (THE INFINITY: UNTOUCHABLE, THE INFINITY BREAKS, SIX EYES CANNOT FOLLOW, THE STRONGEST FALLS, HEY... IT'S ME... IT'S VERITY, STOP SMILING, DELETE, A CARTOON CANNOT GET HURT... RIGHT?, YOUR OWN REFLECTION, ONLY ONE OF YOU, BREAK THE MIRROR), THE ZONE, ELITE FINISHER and the comic words of the Cartoon Cat's version (POW! BAM! WHAP! ZONK! BOING! KRAK! WHAM! BLACK FLASH!!).
YUJI'S ULTIMATE: ULTIMATE!, BLACK FLASH! and BLACK FLASH!! (in a normal fight BLACK FLASH! still shows when the punch lands).
STORY: JUJUTSU HIGH over the corridor, THE WHEEL ADAPTS in chapter 3, HONK! over the cars in New York, HA HA HA over Iron Man, STARK TOWER over the window of the lab.

STAYS: what the characters say, their names, the chapter and end cards, FATALITY, the names of the domains and moves, DOUBLE TAP TO SKIP, the signs that are part of the world (NEW YORK, LIVE), the hit counter, and every line you asked for yourself.
A check that lists every text drawn during every cutscene confirmed that none of the removed words is drawn any more; the game scan found no errors.

t: FREDDY: STRETCHED PUNCHES, GROUND SLAM AND A FATALITY
n: STRETCHED PUNCH: when the enemy is farther than 60 px (the distance where Sukuna's M1 turns into a ranged attack) Freddy's M1 is no longer a slash: his striped sleeve shoots out as far as the Cartoon Cat's glove reaches (the same reach numbers: an enemy 82 to 90 px away is hit, depending on who he is). The first press is the LEFT hand (a bare fist that comes out from behind his body while the glove stays up as a guard, 10 damage), the next press is the RIGHT hand (the clawed glove goes out, 12 damage), then the left again; after 1.4 s without a press it starts with the left hand again. The button says L.PUNCH or R.PUNCH. Closer than 60 px the two slashes are what they were (between about 37 and 60 px neither of them reaches yet). The punches follow every rule of a normal blow: a guard stops them, a dodge misses, a crouching enemy ducks them, they count for the combo meter and FLOW. Not in the Wi-Fi fight.

GROUND SLAM: crouch and press BLUE (the button now says STONES, or BREAK in the skyscraper; 25 cursed energy, 0.9 s before the next one). Freddy springs up out of the crouch (nothing of the enemy's reaches him in the air), comes down on his claw hand and drives it into the ground. ON THE STREET the road cracks towards the enemy, four chunks fly up, and he picks them up and throws them at the enemy one after the other (6 damage and a flinch each; a crouching enemy ducks them, a dodge makes them miss, a guard does not stop them; anyone within 30 px of the fist takes 6 more). IN THE SKYSCRAPER the floor breaks under BOTH of them, two floors deep: both fall (the camera falls for 1.3 s with them, the enemy hangs in the air next to him, a fall costs 3% of health a floor for each of them and never kills) and the whole time Freddy grabs what is around him, the five nearest pieces of furniture of the room (broken floor if the room has fewer), and chucks them quickly at the enemy: 5 damage plus the piece's own (a desk 9, a chair 7, a computer 6, a safe 19) and a flinch each. In the lobby, in the elevator and with the enemy on another floor it is the street move. Standing BLUE is still the boiling water.

FATALITY: when the enemy is at 20% health or less and close, press FATAL (key H, 50% cursed energy, the same rules as everybody's). Freddy runs up and grabs the enemy by the ankles (the bones crunch), yanks his legs up so he flips over and hangs upside down, and SLAMS him on the ground. Then he gets down on ALL FOURS at the enemy's feet, roars, bites the front leg and rips it off, eats it, does the same with the other leg and keeps eating the enemy alive while he screams. He bites his belly, the organs spill out onto him and he eats them too, the enemy's screaming stops, and Freddy gets up and WIPES HIS MOUTH twice with the back of his hand and laughs. It works against Gojo, Yuji, Verity and the Cat (about 17 s); the enemy is gone afterwards and the road keeps a pool of blood. It follows SETTINGS > GAME > GRAPHIC DAMAGE: FULL shows everything, CLEAN is the same without any blood or organs (pale stumps), OFF cuts the middle away: after the slam the screen goes dark and only the sounds play, then it fades in on Freddy standing and wiping his mouth. New sounds: Freddy's growl, roar and cackle, and the wet chewing.
The game scan now plays Freddy's fatality in all three GRAPHIC DAMAGE settings (on three different enemies) and makes him use the ground slam in the skyscraper.

t: ELEVATOR PANEL: THE TEXT FITS INSIDE ITS BUTTONS
n: The floor numbers of the elevator panel were drawn at 16 px in round buttons that are only 24 to 37 px wide, so a number like 50 or 49 stuck out of its button and was cut at the edge, and the small room name under it (OFFICE, LOUNGE, SERVER ...) touched the rim. The size that was meant for them was never used (another rule of the panel overruled it). The numbers and the names now follow the size of their button: the number is a bit less than a third of the button (10 px in a 34 px button) and the name a tenth, so both are completely inside it, on every screen size from 568 x 320 up.

The words of the buttons TOP / LOBBY / ENEMY / LAST are a little smaller too, and OPEN / CLOSE / STOP and these four can no longer push a button out of a very narrow panel (a 4:3 screen). The marks on the floor buttons (the red X of a broken elevator, the ! of damage) follow the size of their button as well.
The game scan now measures the elevator panel in the cab and reports it when the text of a button sticks out of its button.

t: BATTLE SCREEN: NO GRADE LABEL, NO CURSED ENERGY NUMBER
n: The GRADE under the enemy's name (GRADE 4, GRADE 3, GRADE 2, SEMI-GRADE 1, GRADE 1, SPECIAL GRADE, and the grade of a curse) is gone from the battle screen. The labels that are not grades stay: TRAINING and CHAPTER 2 in the story fights, WI-FI, the size of a hunt (SMALL HUNT ...), WAVE 2/5 in RUSH, and HARD.

The cursed energy number ('CE 100%') next to your name is gone, so the cursed energy bar shows it alone. The bar still flashes red when a move is refused, but it no longer writes NO CE. BLEED and FEAR (when you have them) now start right after your name.

Nothing else on the screen changed: the health, cursed energy, FLOW (purple) and STAGGER (orange) bars, the names, the round points, the timer, the buttons of the moves and the enemy info. The optional MOVE INFO panel of Settings > TRAIN still lists your ENERGY, and the grade is still picked on the fighter screen and shown on the result screen.

t: THE FLOOR IS A SIGN ON THE WALL
n: SKYSCRAPER: the floor you are on is not written on the screen any more (the 'FLOOR 30' at the top and the big 'FLOOR 30' that popped up when you arrived are gone). It is a SIGN ON THE WALL of the building now: a steel plate with a blue band that says FLOOR over a black panel with the number in warm light. There is one about every 200 px along every floor (a few more on a narrow screen, fewer on a very wide one), so one is nearly always on the screen; they hang below the health bars, on the free spots of the wall, never on a door, an inner wall, a window or behind a tall piece of furniture (a lamp, a shelf, a vending machine, a rack, a glass pane or a pillar). A fighter who stands in front of one hides it, like anything else on the wall.

The number shines through the darkness like the EXIT signs, so you can read it even when every light of the floor is out (the sign also lights the wall round it). When you arrive on a floor (you start the round, take the stairs, fall, are thrown through a ceiling) the signs flash for a moment (a white frame and white digits, and a glow that fades); after a slide of the camera (stairs, falls) they flash when the camera gets there. Leaving the cab does not flash.
The cab keeps the floor display over its doors. The enemy's line ('FOE 23 UP', 'FOE 23 DOWN', 'FOE AT DOORS', 'FOE 23 IN CAB') stays where it was on the screen, it is not about this floor.

t: BATTLE UI CLEAN-UP: CUTSCENES, ENERGY BAR, ELEVATOR WORDS, FATALITY IN A DOMAIN
n: CUTSCENES: while a cutscene of a fight plays, everything that is not part of it disappears: the health bars and names, the buttons at the top left, the touch buttons, the SENSE button, the training numbers and the elevator panel. This covers every FATALITY (yours or the enemy's), every ULTIMATE (the Cat's, Yuji's, Ryu's JUST THIS ONCE, Freddy's DREAM), the JUMPSCARE, FUGA, Sukuna's domain sign, the opening and the end of a DOMAIN (the fight inside the domain keeps its normal screen) and Gojo's blindfold close-ups. Before, Gojo's FATALITY kept the top-left buttons, and the DOMAIN openings, the Cat's ULTIMATE, Freddy's DREAM and Sukuna's domain sign kept everything on the screen. The tap prompts of a cutscene stay.

THE FREE BOX IS GONE, the cursed energy bar shows it instead: when you are free the bar has its normal colour; when you are not (hit, down, stunned or held) it turns to the inverted colour: Gojo's and Yuji's cyan turns red-orange, Verity's yellow blue, the Cat's pink green, Freddy's red cyan, Sukuna's crimson teal, Ryu's blue gold. The numbers next to the box ('DASH 3' and 'ESC 0.5') are gone with it, and the outline of the bar pulses yellow while a DASH can break the combo. The round timer and the seconds on the DASH button stay.

ELEVATOR: the door no longer writes 'JUMP = GET IN', 'CROUCH = GET IN' or 'JUMP = CALL IT' on the screen, and the cab no longer writes 'JUMP = GET OUT'. The stairs do not write 'JUMP = UP 1' and 'CROUCH = DOWN 1' any more either. The keys work exactly as before; 'OUT OF ORDER' and 'IN USE' are still shown.

FATALITY INSIDE A DOMAIN: while your domain is open FATALITY works (the enemy at 20% health or less and close): Gojo in the Infinite Void, Yuji in the Hometown, Sukuna in the Malevolent Shrine. The domain ends when the cutscene starts and its button starts the cooldown. During the opening of the domain, while your controls are locked, the press still has to wait.

t: NEW FIGHTER SCREEN: TRAINING, BATTLE, WIFI AND A MAP SCREEN
n: BATTLES now opens three big cards: TRAINING, BATTLE and WIFI. WIFI is the old WI-FI ROOMS card, so the mode screen now has CHALLENGES, BATTLES and STORY MODE.

The fighter screen is new and works like Mortal Kombat and Dragon Ball FighterZ: 3 faces on top (GOJO, YUJI, RYU) and 4 below (VERITY, CAT, FREDDY, SUKUNA). Tap a face to put the cursor on it: that face comes alive and the fighter shows big on the side in his idle animation, on a stage in his own colour, with his name, a tag and three of his moves. Tap the same face again or press SELECT to choose him. RANDOM runs the cursor over the fighters you may pick and lands on one (SELECT then chooses him). You choose on the left (red frame), then the enemy on the right (blue frame).

TRAINING: you, then the enemy (Gojo, Yuji, Verity or the Cat), then the map. Every fighter, Gojo too, now starts in a normal training room against the enemy you chose (SETTINGS > TRAIN > ENEMY IS follows your choice). The old free play in the street with the bystanders (Gojo, no enemy) is the yellow FREE PLAY IN THE CITY button, shown when Gojo is your fighter.

BATTLE: the old Versus mode on the same screen: you, then the enemy, with the six grades in a row under the faces (a grade you have not unlocked stays greyed), then the map, START and a VS splash before the fight (a tap skips it). Sukuna and Ryu are greyed (TRAIN ONLY) and Freddy cannot be the enemy yet; fighters you have not bought stay locked.
MAP SCREEN: two big pictures, the street and the skyscraper (taken from the game's own art), with your two fighters standing in them. A tap picks the map, START begins. The old MAP buttons are gone.

The Wi-Fi room's fighter screen has the same look (faces, your fighter on the left, the opponent on the right once you both chose, RANDOM). Only Gojo, Yuji, Verity, the Cat and Freddy can be chosen online. The network code is the old one.
The back button (and Esc) steps back: VS splash, map screen, enemy, your fighter, the three cards, the mode screen. Your last picks are remembered.

t: M1 PUNCHES OVER 15 NOW DEAL 8
n: Every M1 punch or kick that would deal MORE THAN 15 damage now deals exactly 8, for every fighter, yours and the enemy's: Gojo (the elbow, the kick, the walking combo and the red mode's blows), Yuji (the downslam, the spin punch, the hooks when cursed energy is on), Verity (the last M1 punch used to hit for 35, plus 25 more as a combo finisher), Freddy Krueger (his slashes when the extras add up), the Cartoon Cat, Sukuna (his face kick, 16 before) and Ryu (his jump punch 18, downslam 17 and hard punch 16 before).

The rule looks at the final hit, after every bonus: the random extra, the combo finisher, cursed energy, the counter, the heavy swing, OPEN, FLOW and the enemy's grade. A hit of 15 or less is left as it is. The specials are not touched: BLUE and MODE moves, the Black Flash, DIVERGENT FIST, the pierce, the bite, the counters, the FATALITY, the DOMAINS and the ULTIMATES, and the curses' own blows.
Side effect to know about: with cursed energy on (x1.3 damage) most M1 hits go over 15 and become 8, so they are weaker than without it. Tell me if you want the cap to work another way.

t: CHAPTER 5 GOES ON: STARK TOWER
n: Chapter 5 goes on after the black. Yuji opens his eyes (the lids open a little, shut, then open wide) and lies in a glass cell in Stark Tower with Iron Man standing outside, watching. "WHERE AM I?" - "THIS IS STARK TOWER." Yuji gets up and punches the glass: nothing happens (a ring runs over the glass and it rings).

TONY STARK walks in without his suit: the Iron Man that Yuji has been talking to was only the suit (it powers down when Tony arrives). "HEY." - "SO HOW DID YOU COME HERE?" Yuji starts to answer, then STEVE ROGERS walks in (blond, in a jacket): "WHO IS THIS?" - "SOMEONE FROM A DIFFERENT UNIVERSE." Tony opens the chamber, Yuji walks out, and Tony steps into the suit (a scanner runs up him as the armour closes round him): "FOLLOW ME."

Then the HUGE room: a wide shot of a hall that makes the two of them tiny, and the camera comes in. "DO YOU HAVE A PHOBIA OF LARGE PLACES?" - "NO." Tony charges and the ring closes on Yuji like before: TAP anywhere on the screen, or press any key. A good tap: Yuji ducks under the punch and everything goes into SLOW MOTION: Tony's arm, back and one leg dead straight, the other knee bent, looking down at Yuji. A miss: the punch throws Yuji across the room into the wall and he lies there hurt (the blood follows GRAPHIC DAMAGE; with it OFF the blow is cut away).

END OF CHAPTER 5 and TO BE CONTINUED now come after this part. SKIP goes road -> black, lab -> huge room (the tap counts as made), huge room -> the cards. Still no music (the song is coming): new sounds for the panel, the door and the suit.

t: CHAPTER 5: THE IRON MAN
n: Chapter 5 is here: THE IRON MAN. It opens in the chapter list when you finish chapter 4 (CONTINUE takes you there too) and starts right where chapter 4 stopped: Yuji and Iron Man on the freeway in New York, the blade at Yuji's chest. There is no music yet (a song is coming): the wind, the hits, the boots' thrusters and the repulser carry it.

Yuji says "AND IF I DON'T?" and Iron Man answers "WELL... THEN I WILL HAVE TO END YOU."
